answer: A research archive holds nebula images and yarrow trial data. Assign disjoint shards to registered keys and award votes by shard bytes served in random audits. At the audit signal, auditors request unpredictable chunks with a deadline; signed receipts bind the key, shard, round and bytes delivered. Validators accept each shard once per round. Splitting an archive across keys creates no extra weight. More weight needs more distinct data served. Colluding auditors can forge receipts.
